newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed gets Japan deal, awaits UAE decision.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed gets Japan deal, awaits UAE decision.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp said Friday it has begun the production phase of the F-2 fighter plane for the Japan Air Self Defense Force with the award of a $75 million contract from prime contractor, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd.

The initial award is the first part of what could amount to $2.5 billion in contracts to Lockheed over the coming 15-years. Japan plans to buy 130 F-2 aircraft with deliveries to start in 1999 and continue through 2011.

The fighter is based on the F-16, which was originally developed by Lockheed for use by the U.S. Air Force. The contract follows the recent approval by the U.S. Congress of the Japan production program.

Meanwhile Lockheed is awaiting word on another F-16 fighter contract. Lockheed is a finalist with France's Dassault Aviation in the much coveted contract to provide the United Arab Emirates with 80 long-range fighter planes.
The deal is worth between $6 billion to $8 billion.
"We have not received any word from the UAE regarding their final selection," said Kathryn Hayden, spokeswoman for Lockheed.
"The U.S. government is negotiating some of the issues with (the UAE) and we feel that that is making some progress," she added.
A decision is expected before the end of the year.
Lockheed offered a variety of configurations on the F-16 while Dassault is offering its Rafale fighter. The UAE already has 36 Dassault Mirages in its fleet.

The French government has been lobbying hard for sales of the Rafale, which will not go into fleet service until 1999, in the hope of pushing down unit costs of the new fighter. The Rafale has also been offered to Norway and South Korea.
